```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

Chudasama et al. (2026) built a population pharmacokinetic / tumor growth
inhibition (PK-TGI) model for enfortumab vedotin, an anti-Nectin-4
antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) carrying monomethyl auristatin E, in patients
with locally advanced or metastatic urothelial cancer. They used it to ask how
dose reductions, dose eliminations, lower starting doses and early
discontinuations change the simulated tumor response.

The TGI part is a Claret-type model. The tumor sum of diameters (SOD) grows
exponentially and shrinks at a rate driven by the conjugated-ADC plasma
concentration through an Emax term. A resistance rate damps the shrinkage
over time, and a residual FLOOR effect keeps it from reaching zero:

d/dt(SOD) = KG * SOD - KS * (FLOOR + exp(-lambda * t)) * C_ADC / (IC50 + C_ADC) * SOD

The ADC concentration comes from the enfortumab vedotin population PK model of
Zuo et al. (2024), a linear three-compartment model. Chudasama 2026 drove the
TGI with each patient's post hoc PK parameters from that model. A library
model has to simulate new patients, so this file carries the Zuo 2024 final
ADC model in full: typical values, all covariates, IIV and residual error, all
held fixed.

```{r model-info}
mod <- readModelDb("Chudasama_2026_enfortumab")
ui <- rxode2::rxode(mod)
```

* Citation: `r ui$reference`
* Description: `r ui$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/jcph.70241> (open access, PMC13377668)
* PK layer: Zuo et al. 2024, <https://doi.org/10.1002/cpt.3383>

# Population

The TGI analysis set has 603 patients with urothelial cancer from four trials:
EV-101 (phase 1, 0.5-1.25 mg/kg), EV-102 (phase 1, Japan, 1.0-1.25 mg/kg),
EV-201 (phase 2, two cohorts, 1.25 mg/kg) and EV-301 (phase 3, 1.25 mg/kg). All
patients received enfortumab vedotin on days 1, 8 and 15 of a 28-day cycle
(3Q4W); 91.4% started at 1.25 mg/kg. Patients without a post-baseline tumor
assessment were excluded, and so were seven patients whose post-baseline SOD
was 0 mm. The analysis used 2167 SOD observations.

Median (range) age was 68 (24-90) years, body weight 74.2 (36.9-158) kg and
baseline SOD 64.1 (11-331) mm. 74.6% of patients were male and 70.0% were
non-Asian. 15.4% had albumin below 35 g/L, 22.4% had hemoglobin below
100 g/L, and 29.9% had received three or more prior lines of therapy
(Chudasama 2026 Results and Table S10). The Zuo 2024 PK model was estimated
on 748 patients from five studies with the same median age (68 years) and a
median weight of 75 kg.

# Virtual cohort

The same 200 virtual patients are used in every dosing scenario below, so the
scenarios differ only in dosing. Covariates are drawn to match the medians,
means, SDs and ranges of Chudasama 2026 Table S10. All patients get the
reference manufacturing process and laboratory (`FORM_ENFORTUMAB_PROCESSA = 0`,
`ASSAY_LAB_INTERTEK = 0`). Each patient's random effects are drawn once from
the model's IIV variances and passed to every scenario as data columns.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20261114)
n_sub <- 200

rtrunc_norm <- function(n, mean, sd, lo, hi) {
  pmin(pmax(rnorm(n, mean, sd), lo), hi)
}

omega <- ui$omega
cohort <- tibble(
  id = seq_len(n_sub),
  WT = rtrunc_norm(n_sub, 75.8, 17.4, 36.9, 158),
  AGE = rtrunc_norm(n_sub, 67.1, 9.84, 24, 90),
  ALB = rtrunc_norm(n_sub, 38.5, 4.16, 25, 51),
  HGB = rtrunc_norm(n_sub, 113, 15.9, 79, 172),
  # Table S10: median 64.1 mm, mean 76.6 mm -> lognormal sdlog = sqrt(2 * log(76.6 / 64.1))
  TUMSZ = pmin(pmax(rlnorm(n_sub, log(64.1), sqrt(2 * log(76.6 / 64.1))), 11), 331),
  SEXF = rbinom(n_sub, 1, 0.254),
  LINE_4L_PLUS = rbinom(n_sub, 1, 0.299),
  FORM_ENFORTUMAB_PROCESSA = 0L,
  ASSAY_LAB_INTERTEK = 0L,
  etalp = rnorm(n_sub, 0, sqrt(omega["etalp", "etalp"])),
  etalic50 = rnorm(n_sub, 0, sqrt(omega["etalic50", "etalic50"])),
  etalcl = rnorm(n_sub, 0, sqrt(omega["etalcl", "etalcl"])),
  etalvc = rnorm(n_sub, 0, sqrt(omega["etalvc", "etalvc"])),
  etalvp2 = rnorm(n_sub, 0, sqrt(omega["etalvp2", "etalvp2"]))
)

cohort |>
  summarise(
    `Weight median (kg)` = median(WT),
    `Age median (y)` = median(AGE),
    `Albumin median (g/L)` = median(ALB),
    `Hemoglobin median (g/L)` = median(HGB),
    `Baseline SOD median (mm)` = median(TUMSZ),
    `Female (%)` = 100 * mean(SEXF),
    `>= 3 prior lines (%)` = 100 * mean(LINE_4L_PLUS)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
```

# Dosing scenarios

Doses are 1.25 mg/kg (capped at 125 mg) as 30-minute infusions on days 1, 8
and 15 of each 28-day cycle, for six cycles (24 weeks), matching the
simulation horizon of Chudasama 2026 Figures 4-7. Tumor size is computed
daily.

```{r scenarios}
cycle_days <- c(0, 7, 14)
dose_rows <- function(mgkg_by_cycle, skip = character()) {
  out <- expand.grid(cycle = seq_along(mgkg_by_cycle), day = cycle_days)
  out$time <- (out$cycle - 1) * 28 + out$day
  out$mgkg <- mgkg_by_cycle[out$cycle]
  out$tag <- paste0("C", out$cycle, "D", out$day + 1)
  out <- out[out$mgkg > 0 & !(out$tag %in% skip), ]
  out[order(out$time), c("time", "mgkg")]
}

scenarios <- list(
  "1.25 mg/kg 3Q4W" = dose_rows(rep(1.25, 6)),
  "1.00 mg/kg 3Q4W" = dose_rows(rep(1.00, 6)),
  "Reduced to 1.00 mg/kg at Cycle 3" = dose_rows(c(1.25, 1.25, rep(1.00, 4))),
  "Eliminated C1D15 and C2D15" = dose_rows(rep(1.25, 6), skip = c("C1D15", "C2D15")),
  "Discontinued at Cycle 3" = dose_rows(c(1.25, 1.25, 0, 0, 0, 0)),
  "Discontinued at Cycle 5" = dose_rows(c(1.25, 1.25, 1.25, 1.25, 0, 0))
)

obs_times <- seq(0, 168, by = 1)
build_events <- function(doses, label, scen_index) {
  dose_df <- tidyr::crossing(cohort["id"], doses) |>
    left_join(cohort[, c("id", "WT")], by = "id") |>
    mutate(amt = pmin(mgkg * WT, 125), dur = 30 / 1440, evid = 1L, cmt = "central") |>
    select(id, time, amt, dur, evid, cmt)
  # Observation rows sit on the tumor_size state, one of the two declared
  # endpoints; Cc is returned as a column at every row.
  obs_df <- tidyr::crossing(cohort["id"], time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(amt = 0, dur = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "tumor_size")
  bind_rows(dose_df, obs_df) |>
    left_join(cohort, by = "id") |>
    mutate(scenario = label, id = id + (scen_index - 1) * n_sub) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}
events <- bind_rows(Map(build_events, scenarios, names(scenarios), seq_along(scenarios)))
```

# Simulation

Random effects are supplied as data, so the solve uses the model with its IIV
and residual error set to zero.

```{r simulate}
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(ui)
sim <- suppressWarnings(
  # rxode2 warns that a multi-subject solve has no omega; the per-subject
  # random effects are the eta columns of the event data.
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events = events, keep = c("scenario", "TUMSZ"))
) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(
    week = time / 7,
    chg_mm = tumor_size - TUMSZ,
    pchg = 100 * chg_mm / TUMSZ,
    responder = pchg <= -30
  )
stopifnot(!anyNA(sim$tumor_size), nrow(sim) == length(scenarios) * n_sub * length(obs_times))
```

# ADC exposure: PKNCA check of cycle 1

Chudasama 2026 quotes the population-PK estimated cycle 1 Cavg of enfortumab
vedotin as 3.93 (printed as ng/mL; the ADC concentration and IC50 are in
ug/mL throughout the paper, and 3.93 ug/mL is consistent with this model, so
the unit is a typo). The PKNCA check below re-solves the base-case arm over
the first 28 days on a dense grid (every 0.05 day plus the end of each
infusion), because the daily grid used for the tumor curves misses the
end-of-infusion peaks and would understate the AUC.

```{r pknca}
pk_dose <- events |>
  filter(scenario == "1.25 mg/kg 3Q4W", evid == 1, time < 28) |>
  select(id, time, amt, dur, evid, cmt, scenario)
pk_obs <- tidyr::crossing(
  cohort["id"],
  time = sort(unique(c(seq(0, 28, by = 0.05), cycle_days + 30 / 1440)))
) |>
  mutate(amt = 0, dur = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "tumor_size", scenario = "1.25 mg/kg 3Q4W")
pk_events <- bind_rows(pk_dose, pk_obs) |>
  left_join(cohort, by = "id") |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
pk_sim <- suppressWarnings(
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events = pk_events, keep = "scenario")
) |>
  as.data.frame()
pk_conc <- pk_sim |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, scenario)
conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(pk_conc, Cc ~ time | scenario + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(pk_dose, amt ~ time | scenario + id)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 28, cav = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~scenario, ~cav,
  "1.25 mg/kg 3Q4W", 3.93
)
nca_cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "scenario",
  units = c(cav = "ug/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(nca_cmp)

cav_med <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "cav") |>
  pull(PPORRES) |>
  median()
# Structural check on the ADC PK layer: a mis-transcribed clearance, volume
# or dose unit moves the cohort median Cavg by far more than 20%.
stopifnot(abs(cav_med / 3.93 - 1) < 0.2)
```

The simulated cycle 1 Cavg of `r signif(cav_med, 3)` ug/mL lies within
`r round(100 * abs(cav_med / 3.93 - 1))`% of the published 3.93.

```{r pk-plot, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4, fig.cap = "Simulated enfortumab vedotin (ADC) concentrations, 1.25 mg/kg 3Q4W, median and 10th-90th percentiles (compare Chudasama 2026 Figure 4a)."}
sim |>
  filter(scenario %in% c("1.25 mg/kg 3Q4W", "Reduced to 1.00 mg/kg at Cycle 3")) |>
  group_by(scenario, week) |>
  summarise(med = median(Cc), lo = quantile(Cc, 0.1), hi = quantile(Cc, 0.9), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(week, med, colour = scenario, fill = scenario)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.2, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Time (weeks)", y = "ADC concentration (ug/mL)", colour = NULL, fill = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

The concentrations are sampled once a day, so the end-of-infusion peaks
(about 25 ug/mL for a typical patient) fall between grid points.

# Tumor dynamics under the dosing scenarios

Chudasama 2026 counts a simulated patient as a responder at a time point when
the simulated SOD is at least 30% below baseline. The curves below summarise
the same quantities as Figures 4-7: the median change in SOD from baseline in
mm (the figures' 'Relative SOD (mm)' axis) and the percentage of responders,
against the 1.25 mg/kg base case.

The summaries follow the authors' simulation code (Table S5): a time point
with a simulated SOD more than 20% above baseline after week 8 is dropped
(the patient would have stopped treatment for progression), which shapes the
SOD-change percentiles, while the percentage of responders keeps every patient
in the denominator.

```{r summaries}
tgi_sum <- sim |>
  group_by(scenario, week) |>
  summarise(
    resp = 100 * sum(responder) / n_sub,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  left_join(
    sim |>
      filter(!(pchg > 20 & time > 56)) |>
      group_by(scenario, week) |>
      summarise(
        med = median(chg_mm),
        lo = quantile(chg_mm, 0.1),
        hi = quantile(chg_mm, 0.9),
        .groups = "drop"
      ),
    by = c("scenario", "week")
  )

plot_scen <- function(keep, title) {
  d <- filter(tgi_sum, scenario %in% keep)
  base <- filter(d, scenario == "1.25 mg/kg 3Q4W")
  p1 <- ggplot(d, aes(week, med, colour = scenario, linetype = scenario)) +
    geom_ribbon(data = base, aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), fill = "salmon", alpha = 0.2, colour = NA) +
    geom_line() +
    labs(x = "Time (weeks)", y = "Change in SOD from baseline (mm)", title = title, colour = NULL, linetype = NULL) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.direction = "vertical")
  p2 <- ggplot(d, aes(week, resp, colour = scenario, linetype = scenario)) +
    geom_line() +
    labs(x = "Time (weeks)", y = "Patients with >= 30% SOD reduction (%)", colour = NULL, linetype = NULL) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.direction = "vertical")
  list(p1, p2)
}
```

## Comparison with the published curves

The published values below were read off Chudasama 2026 Figures 5-7 by the
maintainers (percentage of responders and median change in SOD from baseline
in mm, both at week 24).

```{r compare}
wk24 <- tgi_sum |>
  filter(week == 24) |>
  select(scenario, resp, med)
published_wk24 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~scenario, ~resp_pub, ~med_pub,
  "1.25 mg/kg 3Q4W", 58, -23,
  "1.00 mg/kg 3Q4W", 54, -21,
  "Eliminated C1D15 and C2D15", 50, -19,
  "Discontinued at Cycle 3", 37.5, -12,
  "Discontinued at Cycle 5", 50.5, -20
)
wk24 |>
  left_join(published_wk24, by = "scenario") |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Scenario = scenario,
    `Responders, simulated (%)` = resp,
    `Responders, Chudasama 2026 (%)` = resp_pub,
    `Median change, simulated (mm)` = med,
    `Median change, Chudasama 2026 (mm)` = med_pub
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)

r24 <- setNames(wk24$resp, wk24$scenario)
# Every scenario gives each virtual patient no more drug than the base case,
# and the shrinkage term increases with concentration, so with the same
# patients in every arm the base case has the most responders. The ordering
# is deterministic, not a sampling result.
stopifnot(
  r24["1.25 mg/kg 3Q4W"] >= r24["1.00 mg/kg 3Q4W"],
  r24["1.25 mg/kg 3Q4W"] >= r24["Eliminated C1D15 and C2D15"],
  r24["Discontinued at Cycle 5"] >= r24["Discontinued at Cycle 3"],
  # Envelope on the base-case response rate (published about 58%).
  r24["1.25 mg/kg 3Q4W"] > 40, r24["1.25 mg/kg 3Q4W"] < 75
)
```

The virtual cohort reproduces the direction and the relative size of every
published scenario effect: a lower starting dose and early dose eliminations
cost a few percentage points of responders, a reduction at Cycle 3 costs
almost nothing, and stopping at Cycle 3 costs far more than stopping at
Cycle 5. The absolute response rates and median shrinkage run a few points
below the published curves, which were simulated from the post hoc estimates
of the 603 trial patients rather than from the population distributions (see
Assumptions and deviations).

## Best overall change (Table S7)

Table S7 compares the observed proportion of patients whose best change from
baseline was a decrease of more than 30% with simulations of the analysis
dataset. The simulations used each patient's actual dosing and sampling
history; the closest analogue here is the base case over 24 weeks.

```{r table-s7}
best <- sim |>
  filter(scenario == "1.25 mg/kg 3Q4W") |>
  group_by(id) |>
  summarise(best = min(pchg), .groups = "drop")
tibble::tibble(
  Source = c("This model, 1.25 mg/kg 3Q4W, 24 weeks", "Table S7, all studies, simulated", "Table S7, all studies, observed"),
  `Best decrease > 30% (%)` = c(100 * mean(best$best < -30), 53.8, 57.0)
) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **PK layer from Zuo 2024.** Chudasama 2026 drove the TGI with individual
  post hoc PK parameters (control-stream columns CLD, V1, Q2D, V2, Q3D, V3)
  rather than with a population PK model. To simulate new patients, this file
  carries the Zuo 2024 final ADC population PK model (Table 1) with all of its
  covariates, IIV and residual error. All PK parameters are fixed. The paper
  cites this model as reference 10.
* **Zuo 2024 covariate forms.** Zuo 2024 states that continuous covariates
  enter as power functions of the covariate over its median and categorical
  covariates as proportional changes. The reference values (75 kg, 68 years,
  albumin 39 g/L, hemoglobin 112 g/L, SOD 65 mm, male) are those of its
  reference population (Figure 2 legend, where albumin is misprinted as
  "39 g/mL"). The weight exponent printed for "CLA, Q2, Q3" is applied to all
  three clearances, and the one for "V1, V2, V3" to all three volumes.
* **Zuo 2024 IIV.** Reported as CV%; converted with omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2). No
  correlations are reported, so the IIV is diagonal.
* **Zuo 2024 residual error.** Proportional plus additive, combined in the
  nlmixr2 default form; Zuo 2024 does not say how the two were combined.
* **Manufacturing process and analytical laboratory.** Zuo 2024 estimated
  effects of manufacturing process A on clearance and of the Intertek
  laboratory on V3. Both indicators are 0 in all simulations here.
* **TGI final estimates.** Values are from Table S9 (final model, 603
  patients). The NONMEM control stream in Table S3 lists initial estimates,
  and the mrgsolve code in Table S4 agrees with Table S9 except for the IC50
  IIV variance (3.57 in the code, 3.51 in Table S9); Table S9 is used. Table S8
  (610 patients including complete responders) and Table S12 (SAEM
  re-estimation) are sensitivity analyses and are not packaged.
* **Prior lines of therapy.** The Results text says ">3 prior lines", but the
  Methods ("3+ lines vs all others"), Table S9 ("Prior therapies (3+)") and
  the code define the category as three or more, which is what the
  `LINE_4L_PLUS` indicator encodes. The reference level pools zero, one and
  two prior lines.
* **Cycle 1 Cavg unit.** The Results quote the cycle 1 Cavg as "3.93 ng/mL";
  the ADC concentrations and IC50 are in ug/mL everywhere else in the paper,
  and the model reproduces 3.93 ug/mL, so ng/mL is a typo.
* **Time origin.** The resistance term uses time since the first dose
  (NONMEM `T`, mrgsolve `SOLVERTIME`), not time since the last dose.
* **Simulation design.** Chudasama 2026 simulated the 603 analysis patients
  from their post hoc parameter estimates. This vignette uses a 200-patient
  virtual cohort with random effects drawn from the IIV variances, so the
  joint distribution of covariates, KG and IC50 differs from that of the
  trial patients. The IC50 variance (3.51) is large, so a cohort drawn from
  it spreads further than one built from shrunken post hoc estimates. The
  week-8 progression filter and the responder denominator follow the authors'
  Shiny code (Table S5).
* **Figure values.** The week-24 response rates and median changes quoted
  from Figures 5-7 were read off the published plots and are approximate.
* **Covariate distributions.** Truncated normal draws for weight, age,
  albumin and hemoglobin and a truncated lognormal for baseline SOD, matched
  to the Table S10 summaries; the joint correlation of covariates is not
  reported and is not reproduced.
